newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Mexico's Zedillo arrives in Seoul to boost trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo arrives in Seoul to boost trade.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo arrived in Seoul on Thursday in a bid to boost trade contacts and drum up investment for his struggling economy.
During his three-day visit to South Korea, Zedillo will hold summit talks with President Kim Young-sam and meet top business representatives, the South Korean Foreign Ministry said.
It is the first visit by a Mexican head of state.

As part of Zedillo's visit, South Korea's Export-Import Bank on Friday will grant a $10 million credit line to Banco de Comercio Exterior (Bancomext) to promote technology transfers and the import of South Korean capital goods to Mexico, the Mexico Embassy said in a statement.

A memorandum between the Electronics Industries Association of Korea and its Mexican counter part, CANIECE, will be signed on Friday as will a cooperation agreement between the Association of Foreign Trade Agents of Korea and Bancomext.
A protocol between the Federation of Korea Industries, a grouping of major South Korean companies, and its Mexican counterpart, the Confederation of Industrial Chambers, will also be signed.
In 1995, Mexico suffered its worst recession in half a century. A devaluation of the peso in December 1994 triggered the crisis, in which more than a million people lost their jobs.
Soaring interest rates drove millions more into debt.
The trip to South Korea is the last leg of Zedillo's Asian visit, which took him to Beijing, Singapore and the APEC conference in Manila.
